Censorship is the control of the information and ideas circulated within a society either on a website or somewhere else. Removing content that is illegal is definitely not censorship. In fact, keeping it is censoring the obvious rule of law. In a society where censorship is minimal, all information is permissible unless against the law. So, where can content removal be justified?

While based of freedom, a truly free society cannot dispense it's members of responsibility. The more responsible a society is, the least rules it has. Therefore, a responsible member should be able to know what to do, and where to do it.

If illegal content can have it's way, in a way or another, to its audience, the same can happen to legal content. So, as long as the content is legal, it should be available in its assigned place. An information that is totally irrelevant to its destination can obviously be subject to removal, and redirected to a more appropriate destination.

As for abiding to a certain set of rules, we should clarify what kind of rule it is. A society is shaped by it members, and it's up to them to set the specific rules that should apply to them. A society becomes abusive when its rules go against the consensus of members, in the interest of a limited number of people. The defined set of specific rules has to be legal (as for the general legality above), justified (and not leonine or arbitrary), fair (takes into consideration various opinions and admits reversal), and transparent (public ruling).

I think how you have phrased it is the best way to have done so. You clearly defined censorship, and I think that is a very important point, since there can be differing views on what censorship is.

The demonstration of what is right and wrong should also be majorly agreed upon by the society, which is where issues arise when those in power don't listen to the majority in favour of their own ideals, which could be very corrupt.

One fuzzy aspect of censorship that often gets overlooked is spam advertising. None of us like it. None of us want it. I would (and will) remove it from any of my subverses. But in reality, are we not suppressing the spammer's "free speech"? Their content is not (usually) illegal. Just annoying and unwanted. But isn't that the underlying basis for the censorship of everything from race supremacy to adverse political views? Unwanted opposition to societal norms? Are we being hypocrites when we clamor for free speech and unrestricted exchange of ideas, yet offhandedly dispose of a subculture (spammers?) that we simply find annoying?

I am in no way endorsing spammers. As I said, I won't allow the crap in my subverses. However, I do have to pause and think on the duality of the situation. Just food for thought.

Child porn (not lolicon, two completely different things) and crime planning (bank robberies, murder, etc.) are the only things I feel are actually justified in banning. If it doesn't hurt anybody else, it shouldn't be your problem. That's my take on it, anyways.

I reject out of hand, the idea that words or ideas ever harm people. Actions harm people. Words and ideas are only a representation of actions. Therefore, words and ideas should never be deleted. However, if a type of word or ideas is made illegal and ratified by an overwhelming super-majority of the people, I will then accept the censoring of it.

I don't care about people's feelings. I don't care about their emotional trauma. Hiding and obscuring words or ideas about peoples' feelings or trauma will not eliminate their trauma. It will only bury memory of it for a little while. Censorship keeps society from learning. The answer to bad words and ideas is never fewer words and ideas, it is more words and better ideas.

...if a type of word or ideas is made illegal and ratified by an overwhelming super-majority of the people, I will then accept the censoring of it.

What if the super-majority, in spite of being that, is actually wrong?
As long as it's a legitimate super-majority, then tough shit.

Censorship...yeah, that's usually wrong. The type you're on about is controlling the circulation of information, surely.

And as wrong goes, to me, that's fairly wrong. I could blab on about it for ages and get really off topic, but I'll try and be short. Censorship, historically, has been used to control and manipulate the masses. That's the point. If someone doesn't have all the information, their decisions are altered. If you are controlling what information they do have, you can manipulate their decision making. Sometimes you don't even have to censor, you just stir it up, like the media. How often do you see a story about the good an immigrant has done for his community, compared to the masses of "immigrant involved in benefit fraud" stories? And then there's controlling what they can say as well as read. If what I've read is accurate, that's one of the things going on with Reddit. Mods deciding what people can and cannot say.

Buuut, if banning people from saying certain things itself was proper censorship, then we should all be pissed at any rules. But we're not, so there's clearly a line, and different people draw it in different places.

For me, the moment it becomes censorship is when someone is made to be silent because what they say is "offensive" or "problematic" or damaging to the establishment. I understand, and support, banning people from shitposting. There's a reason it's called shitposting. But when it comes to things like feelings...I can't support banning or censoring words that hurt people's feelings. It's not right. It's dangerous.

I mean, if we're going to assume those in authority know what's best, and we should roll over and accept that, then why don't we consider their opinions from the perspective of someone who it harms? Disregarding Reddit mods, a good real world example is that once upon a time, those in authority thought that women were not equal to men. What if they censored people who tried to claim otherwise? If you remove the people, you have [ ] is censoring [ ] because what [ ] has to say has offended them. It doesn't become alright just because what people are saying may be genuinely offensive. If you set it in stone that it's alright to silence people because you don't like what you're hearing, then you're saying it's alright to do it no matter what - which legitimises censorship in the real world.

As for how far the rules go..I do believe that should be up to each individual subverse. It's not now, nor, I think, will it ever be a black and white matter where you can make one ruling. But, I think that some things it's easy to question. If someone is banned, is there someone they can appeal to who is not involved with the group who banned them? If not, there should be. And probably not only one individual, either or that would be easy to corrupt. Something like a high moderator position, or something. A group of individuals who can judge whether or not a ban was legitimate, and have the person unbanned if they find it wasn't. But then you have the problem of the rules..as I said, each should decide their own, but what if the rules are totally unreasonable?

So then, I think having site rules that all subverses must comply with, and then each subverses rules would be best. These site rules would have to ensure free speech in every sub - for example, one being that you can't ban someone for going against the opinion of the subverses moderators. Things like that. There should not be a subverse where a person feels they will be banned if they express their honest opinion.
